title: Customer-run network smoke tests and upgrade rollout generator for air-gapped/private deployments
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers requesting private/VPC/on-prem installs frequently fail early in onboarding due to subtle network constraints (DNS, ephemeral egress proxies, MTU, corporate TLS interception) and non-deterministic upgrade windows. We need a lightweight, customer-run preflight that produces a deterministic pass/fail artifact and a generated staged rollout plan that respects customer maintenance windows and airgap constraints.

Proposal: Build a two-part product: (1) a small, auditable 'network-smoke' binary/script (container-less) customers can run inside their network to validate connectivity assumptions and collect a signed artifact of checks (TCP/SYN to endpoints, TLS handshake validation against KMS-protected certs, DNS resolution graph, proxy autodetect, MTU/path MTU probe). The binary runs offline and outputs a compressed JSON summary + signed metadata (no raw logs unless customer opts in). (2) An "upgrade rollout generator" service in the Console that ingests the signed artifact and, using customer-provided maintenance windows and risk profile, creates a staged rollout plan (canary percentages, per-region sequencing, rollback triggers tied to monitored metrics) and a suggested validation script runbook for the customer.

Goals: reduce onboarding flips caused by hidden network assumptions, accelerate safe upgrade scheduling for airgapped installs, and provide deterministic artifacts for SRE/ops and Redwood support triage.

Trade-offs considered: (a) Data collection vs privacy: we favor minimal metadata and cryptographic signing; raw logs remain local by default. (b) Complexity vs adoption: prefer single small binary with extensible plugin points rather than complex agent. (c) Online vs offline artifact submission: support both direct upload to Console via pre-signed URL and manual upload through support channels.

Out-of-scope for initial MVP: automated remediation (we only surface and suggest steps), deep packet inspection checks, and containerized agent rollout.

Stakeholders: Maya Chen (PM), Liam O'Connor (Tech PM/Eng lead liaison), Priya Nair (Support), Diego Alvarez (SRE), Ravi Patel (Security).
acceptance_criteria: Network-smoke artifact schema v1 documented in Confluence and validated by SRE/security
Executable (Linux x86_64) that runs without root and performs TCP/DNS/TLS/MTU checks and produces a signed artifact
Console UI flow that accepts artifact upload and returns a staged rollout plan PDF and JSON within 5 minutes
Generated rollout plan includes canary sequencing, per-region grouping, maintenance window adherence, and explicit rollback triggers
Security sign-off obtained for data collected and signing approach
Integration test: run artifact from a test airgapped VM in our lab, upload, and verify generated plan matches expected golden file
comments: 2026-02-12 - Discovery: interviewed three enterprise customers (finance, healthcare, manufacturing). Common failures: TLS interception, corporate proxies rewriting SNI, and blocked ephemeral egress during upgrades.
2026-02-18 - Design sync with SRE: agreed on minimal artifact containing summary metrics and certificate fingerprints; raw packet captures are opt-in only.
2026-02-25 - Engineering spike (ENG-1842): prototype binary performs DNS chain resolution and TLS handshake validation; initial runtime <3s for core checks.
2026-03-01 - PM review: choice to support both pre-signed upload and manual upload approved to respect airgap policies.
2026-03-05 - Security: requested HSM/KMS flow for signing keys and threat model for artifact submission. Security review scheduled.
2026-03-10 - UX: mockups for Console upload page and generated PDF reviewed; added a step for customer to annotate maintenance windows and risk tolerance.
2026-03-12 - Blocker: awaiting legal approval on data retention language for artifacts for EU customers. Action: Priya to engage legal and propose 30-day retention default with opt-out.

2026-03-15 - Next steps: finalize artifact schema doc, complete signing prototype using KMS, and scope engineering sprint for binary hardening and Console ingestion pipeline.
